description: Glitch Armor is a protective spell inspired by the nuanced experience of visibility within queer communities. On one hand, being visible allows them to be their full authentic selves, occupy space, exist, and find others alike. On the other hand, being visible exposes them to emotional and physical violence. This 3D animated couple reacts to movement in the room through a live camera feed. In turn, the glitch effect takes place and renders them progressively less visible.
What if technology had evolved to have human personality traits?
What if digital characters also had anxiety about being visibly queer?

Glitch Armor represents an exercise in character design, utilizing interactive technology as another layer for storytelling. As more viewers get closer to the installation, the characters display their personalities, anxiety, and rebellious thoughts.

projects.title: Look Again
description: This project explores 'low-tech' computer vision through a simple Python script. Using the NumPy library and a webcam, it enables the computer to interpret the visual input in a more human-like way. Instead of processing thousands of individual pixels and RGB values, the script simplifies the image data into average colors across larger areas. These are then compared to a small database to identify the closest color match.

gallery.caption: Imported body part as an .fbx file in TD
Opportunity for optimization, all these nodes could be a simpler script

description: *This project needs an update, more in the .txt log.

This is a digital puzzle made of my own 3D scanned body, inspired by academic literature in queer theory. The final piece acts as a manifesto regarding body-related and perception-based societal norms. In the end, I see it as a kind of auto-ethnographic process where I was able to analyze the external perception, as well as my own, of my body, both in a deconstructed and reconstructed state. With MediaPipe, a machine learning tool, the viewer in front of a visual composition of myself with heavy medical and 'objective' undertones can replace the pieces back in place using hand gestures. The experience is complete when the viewer sees the whole manifesto written in the place of a previously dry descriptions of each body parts.

projects.title: Post-Apocalyptic Hottie

gallery.caption: Displacement map used for the ground block

description: This character tells a futuristic story, where fashion is still a priority even after the environment became hostile. I imagine people in this alternate universe having to cover up entirely to protect themselves from the polluted air and intense UV rays.

In this character design exercise, the personal protective equipment takes the shape of a pair of plateform boots, a helmet with anti-UV glasses, a skin-tight shirt to show off defined chest muscles, puffy leather pants and gloves. To complete the outfit, a cute shoulder bag that matches the boots and helmet along wiht a phone capting atmospheric information are added as accessories.
This high-ploygon count sculpted character is brought to life using Mixamo, a motion capture library. The textures are painted and generated with Substance Designer and Substance Painter.

description: This is a low-poly diorama that tells the story of an adored demon toad. The animations are minimal, but still add to the rich story developed through the different animals and plants. The background was generated with Substance Designer, and the rest of the scene was modelled, textured, animated, and lit in Blender 3D.

projects.title: EFFA - Visual Identity

gallery.caption: A few word on the choices of typography, color, and style

description: This visual identity was developped in the context of a graphic design class during my - unfinished - bachelor degree in Industrial Design at Universié de Montréal. We were all prompted to create posters, book covers, and other merchandise for the next iteration of EFFA (Exposition des finissants de la Faculté de l'aménagement).

The theme being 'CTRL+S', I went with a design sporting heavy contrast, fine lines, and repeating typography. My inspiration for these choices came from an exploration of the theme that could be resumed in three words: Nervosité, Écho, and Arts Numériques (translation: Nervousness, Echos, and Digital Arts).

projects.title: Pyre
description: This portable barbecue concept was developped in the context of a class during my - unfinished - bachelor degree in Industrial Design at Universié de Montréal. I was prompted to create this object for the Hudson Bay Company (HBC), and a lot of emphasis was put on the branding. It had be marketed towards their mid-to-high end costumer base, be portable, and safe.

After researching metal sheet bending and assembly, I came up with this sleek and original stackable design. For instance, with just six tabs on the lid and six corresponding notches in the base, the lid securely stays in place. This approach not only provides an elegant form but also ensures that the object's fabrication and assembly are straightforward and cost-effective.

interests.title: 3D Animation
interests.summary: Creating a digital product with 3D software.
interests.description: When I say I do 3D animation, I mean mostly everything that can happen in a 3D software. That's modelling, remeshing, UV mapping, texturing, rigging, animating, lighting, simulating physics, and compositing. Not every project requires all steps, but I deeply enjoy this overall process.

interests.title: Tattooing
interests.summary: Marking the skin permanently with needles and ink.
interests.description: I have always been drawn to the tattoing process, both to decorate my own body and others. I find body modification enticing because it takes effort and pain, making it something significant and giving it grounding properties.

interests.title: Creative Coding
interests.summary: Programming as a tool for creative expression.
interests.description: I started learning to code a few years ago, and I now am pretty decent at HTML/CSS, Javascript, and Python. These languages opened up so many doors for me, and most of my current projects include some kind of script.

interests.title: Interactive Technologies
interests.summary: Systems, devices, or software designed to enable real-time engagement.
interests.description: This is a wide area, but my personal interests lies within cameras (especially webcams), video games, and game mechanics. I experiment with interactive design to tell new kinds of stories, some that may need more nuance or that may benefit from having multiple states revealed to the viewers.
